feature.summary: Shows a reference like [^1] as a small raised marker tied to a note at the bottom of the answer. Web, desktop and Chrome link the marker to a footnotes list with a back-link. Mobile shows a numbered marker, a bottom list, and an alert on tap. VS Code and CLI have no footnote support.

purpose.what_it_does: Links a marker in the text to a note, so an answer can carry side comments without breaking the sentence.
purpose.why_it_exists: Models sometimes use Markdown footnotes. Without support the reader sees literal [^1] text (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md S20.14).
purpose.who_uses_it: Readers of answers that cite or annotate with footnotes.
problems_solved: Raw [^1] markers do not litter the text.
Notes are reachable and the reader can return to the spot (web, Chrome).
Two messages on one page do not clash ids (web).
use_cases: Read an answer with a definition note.
Jump from a marker to its note and back.
Tap a marker on mobile to read the note.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Tauri): markers and a footnotes section at the end of the message (remark-gfm output, MarkdownContent.tsx:339-343, 891-894).

Mobile: marker in text, tap opens an alert titled 'Footnote <n>' (MarkdownInline.tsx:157-159, 410-430), and a 'Footnotes' list at the end of the message (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:876-925, 1672-1675).
Chrome: raised number linking to a section labelled 'Footnotes' with a back-link (markdown.ts:217-246; test side-panel-markdown-parity.test.ts:216-260).
prerequisites: A reply with a footnote reference and a definition line like [^1]: text.
screens_and_controls: Web and Chrome: click the marker to jump; click the back arrow to return.
Mobile: tap the marker (button role when a note exists).
journey: Web and Chrome jump to the list item; mobile opens an alert.
feedback_and_outputs: Mobile alert with the note's plain text.

working: Web and desktop: footnote links stay in the same tab and their target id gets the sanitiser prefix so the jump lands (MarkdownContent.tsx:335-343, 371-378). A per-message scope keeps ids unique (891-894; test MarkdownContent.render.test.tsx:329).

Streaming: a settled block that uses a footnote label is not trusted until the definition arrives; the whole message folds into one unit (StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:22-47, 89-103; test StreamingMarkdownContent.test.tsx:221-235).
Mobile: footnote nodes parse, number and open an alert; a Footnotes section lists referenced notes (MarkdownInline.tsx:410-430; MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1634-1636, 1672-1675).
Chrome: markdown-it-footnote with custom renderers, a labelled section, and a back-link labelled with the note number (markdown.ts:217-246).
incomplete: Mobile list items have no back-link (renderFootnoteSection draws number and text only, MessageContentRenderer.tsx:876-925).
disconnected_or_disabled: The brief's status for mobile and Chrome says missing; the code shows both implemented. The brief status is stale.
not_available: VS Code: no footnote plugin in markdown-it setup (render.ts:16-24); the marker shows as literal text [inferred].
CLI: ENABLE_FOOTNOTES is not in the parser options (markdown_renderer.rs:147-150); marker shows as literal text [inferred].

established.statement: Footnote references ([^1]) render as superscript markers linked to a footnotes section.

acceptance_criteria: 'A[^1]' with '[^1]: note' shows a raised marker and a footnotes list on web and Chrome.

inferred: VS Code and CLI should at least keep the note text readable; today they would show the marker and definition as plain text [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add the footnote plugin to the VS Code renderer reusing the Chrome rules.
[proposed] Print footnote notes at the end of CLI output.
[proposed] Add a back-link on mobile or document that the alert replaces it.

corrections.claim: Mobile: footnote nodes parse, number and open an alert; tap opens an alert titled 'Footnote <n>' (MarkdownInline.tsx:157-159, 410-430)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: showFootnote calls Alert.alert(`Footnote ${n}`, inlinePlainText(note)) (:157-159). That is only the fallback. If context.options.onFootnotePress is supplied, it is called with the label instead (:413, :424). The test MarkdownInline.render.test.tsx:545 exercises that path with a jump callback.
corrections.correction: Tapping a footnote marker on mobile opens an alert titled 'Footnote <n>' unless the caller passes onFootnotePress, in which case that handler runs and no alert shows.

missing_facts: Mobile footnote taps can be overridden by an onFootnotePress option (MarkdownInline.tsx:49,413,424), and a test covers it (MarkdownInline.render.test.tsx:545). The page says the tap always opens an alert.

The page's front matter (implementation mobile/chrome: missing, available_on web+desktop) and its Status table (Mobile and Chrome 'not built') contradict its own body and gaps section, which say mobile and Chrome are built (MarkdownInline.tsx:410-430; markdown.ts:217-246). Section 10's 'Not built on: Mobile, ... Chrome' line repeats the stale claim.

Web footnote parsing is not a footnote-specific plugin: REMARK_PLUGINS (remarkPlugins.ts:71-77) holds remarkGfm, remarkMath, remarkBreaks, remarkLosslessTables and remarkAssistantFenceIdentity. Footnote ids use a clobberPrefix built from footnoteScope (MarkdownContent.tsx:891-894), and unscoped callers get an empty prefix, so uniqueness depends on the caller.
